 :JUDGMENT:
This is a Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- for the death of N Nagabhushana in the Road Traffic Accident occurred on 04.07.2025.
2.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 04.07.2025 at about 6.30 p.m., Nagabhushana @ N Nagabhushana was proceeding from T B Cross side towards Chikkaballapura side by riding TVS XL Motor Cycle bearing No. KA.08.J.9550 and when he reached in front of Madarasa Service road, Bagepalli to Chikkaballapura NH-44 road, Bagepalli taluk,
Chikkaballapura, Karnataka, at that time the driver of Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973
driven the same in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, Nagabhushana sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to injuries on the spot.
Thereafter, the dead body was shifted to Government hospital, Bagepalli, wherein postmortem was conducted and handed over the dead body to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and other incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 33 years, doing coolie work and also fruit business and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioners were entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased.
Due to the sudden death of deceased, the petitioners are put to lot of mental agony and untold misery.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Bus bearing No.
KA.40.F.0973 by its driver.

As such the jurisdictional police have registered a case Nagamani Y O vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12793679/
2 against the said driver in Cr. No. 228/2025 for the offences punishable U/Sec. 281 &
106(1) of BNS.

sentences.text: Respondent being the RC owner and internal insurer of the said bus is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
With these averments petitioners prayed to allow the petition.
3. After service of notice, the respondent appeared through its counsel and filed Written Statement.

4. The averments of written statement of respondent are as under:
This respondent has denied the cause and manner of accident by contending that, the rider of the motor cycle viz. deceased himself fallen on the ground.
As such, the driver of the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 on humanitarian ground stopped the bus to see the fallen position of the deceased.
Due to which the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident.

Further, it has denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased.
With these averments, the respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
: I S S U E S:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that Sri. N Nagabhushana @ Nagabhushana S/o Narasimhappa was died due to injuries sustained in the accident occurred on 04.07.2025 at about 6.30 p.m. due to rash or negligent driving of Bus bearing No.
KA.40.F.0973 by its driver, infront of Madarasa Service road, Bagepalli to Chikkaballapura NH-44 road, Bagepalli taluk, Chikkaballapura, when he was proceeding by riding TVS XL Motor Cycle bearing No. KA.08.J.9550 as alleged in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?

If so, how much and from whom?
4.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as P.W.1 and the documents have been marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
Thereafter, P.W.1 was subject to the process of cross examination.
The driver of the Bus has been examined as R.W.1 and the documents have been marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
R.W.1 was subject to the process of cross- examination.
7. Heard the arguments of both sides.
Perused the materials placed on record.

The findings of the Tribunal to the above referred issues are as under:

sentences.text: Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative Issue No.2 :- In the partly Affirmative.

Issue No.3 :-
In the partly Affirmative.
Issue No.4 :- As per the final order for the following:

:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1 :- Before going to discuss this issue, it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "It is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision of Sunitha and others Vs.
Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2020) 13 SCC 486 observed that, "While deciding cases arising out of Motor Vehicle Accidents, the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not restrict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in Criminal Cases''.

entities.text:
Sunitha and others Vs.
Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2020) 13 SCC 486
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it is crystal clear that the petitioners have to prove their case on the principle of preponderance of probabilities.

9. It is the case of the petitioners that, on 04.07.2025 at about 6.30 p.m., Nagabhushana @ N Nagabhushana was proceeding from T B Cross side towards Chikkaballapura side by riding TVS XL Motor Cycle bearing No. KA.08.J.9550 and when he reached infront of Madarasa Service road,
Bagepalli to Chikkaballapura NH-44 road, Bagepalli taluk, Chikkaballapura, Karnataka, at that time the driver of Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 driven the same in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle from behind and caused the accident.

Due to the said impact,
Nagabhushana sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to injuries on the spot.

In order to prove their contentions, the 1st petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1.
10.
P.W.1 has filed affidavit in lieu of examination in chief and reiterated the petition averments.
In order to prove issue No.1, P.W.1 has produced documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
Ex. P.1
is the true copy of complaint.
Ex. P.2
is the true copy of FIR.
Ex. P.3
is the true copy of spot mahazar.
Ex . P.4
is the true copy of spot sketch.
Ex . P5
is the true copy of vehicle seizure mahazar.
Ex . P6
is the true copy of inquest report.
Ex . P7
is the true copy of PM report.
Ex . P8
is the true copy of IMV report.
Ex . P9

& 
Ex .P10 are the notice and reply to the notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act and Ex.P11 is the true copy of charge sheet.
11. It is the contention of the respondent that, the rider of the motor cycle viz. deceased himself fallen on the ground.
As such, the driver of the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 on humanitarian ground stopped the bus to see the fallen position of the deceased.

Due to which the Bus bearing No.
KA.40.F.0973 has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident.

In order to substantiate their contention, the driver of the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 got examined as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
12.
Now, the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of R Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 by its driver or not?.

In order to answer Nagamani Y O vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12793679/
4 the aspect of rash or negligence, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.4 & Ex.P11 for discussion.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.4, i.e., spot sketch it is evident that, the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 has dashed against the motor cycle in which the deceased was proceeding from behind and caused the accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P11 i.e., charge sheet it discloses that, charge sheet was submitted against the driver of the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 for the offences punishable U/Sec.106(1) & 281 of BNS against the driver of the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973.
13.
Further, the respondent has raised a contention that, deceased himself fallen on the ground.
On perusal of Ex.R1, the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 has got scratches in its left side door beeding.
Therefore, on perusal of Ex.R1 to R3, in can be inferred that the accident took place due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver of the said Bus.

That apart, if the deceased himself fallen on the ground and there is no involvement of the bus in the alleged accident, then the Bus bearing No.
KA.40.F.0973 will not get scratched as mentioned in Ex.R1.
Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to negligent driving of bus driver.

14. Now, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of CIVIL APPEAL NO.
OF 2025 (Arising out of SLP(C) No. 10351/2019) dated 25.02.2025 between Ranjeeth and another Vs. Abdul Kayam Neb and another held that, "once a charge sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.

entities.text: Ranjeeth and another Vs. Abdul Kayam Neb
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even if the eye witnesses are not examined, that will not be fatal to prove the death of the deceased due to negligence of the driver''.

Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs.
Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder: "
Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that, the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
The above referred decisions are squarely applicable to the case on hand.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P7, the deceased Nagabushana has died due to the injuries caused to him in the alleged accident.

15. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the deceased was proceeding by riding motor cycle the driver of Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 driven the same in a rash or negligent manner and caused the accident.
There are no evidence to disbelieve the case of petitioners.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:- This issue is with regard to age and income of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 33 years at the time of his death.
In the instant case, the respondent has disputed the age of the deceased.
In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.12, the notarized copy of Aadhaar card pertaining to deceased Nagabhushana.
On careful perusal of this document, it reveals that, the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1992.
The accident was occurred on 04.07.2025.
Therefore, age of the deceased is 33 years and 6 months at the time of accident.

Therefore, by relying on the judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 5353/2024 (MV-D) decided on 07th August 2025 between The Managing Director, Motor Claims Hub BMTC, Shanthinagar, Bengaluru Vs. Smt. Jyothi and others, this tribunal considered the completed age of petitioner.

Accordingly, the age of the deceased is Nagamani Y O vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12793679/
5 considered as 33 years as on the date of accident.

entities.text: Nagamani Y O vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. Now, the next aspect is with respect to income of deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was doing Coolie work and also doing fruit business and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the respondent has denied the avocation and income of deceased.
It is relevant to note that, the petitioners have not produced documents to show that, the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in a case of Godabai and others Vs. Goudappa and another reported in 2024 SCC Online KAR 15570 (Decided in MFA No. 201022/2018 (MV-D) on 04.06.2024) wherein the Hon'ble Division Bench of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that at para 18 is as here under: "In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority''.

entities.text: Godabai and others Vs. Goudappa and another reported in 2024 SCC Online KAR 15570
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
That apart, the Hon'ble High Court in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

18. In the absence of authentic documents and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the Judgments of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 04.07.2025.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/- per month.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.17,000/- per month by adopting the method given by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
19.
ISSUE No.3:- This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased, petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the minor daughters and petitioner No.4 is the mother of deceased.
The 1st petitioner has lost her husband, petitioner Nos.2 and 3 have lost their loving father and petitioner No.4 has lost her son at her old age.

Hence,
Petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of that there are 4 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4th of the amount is to be deducted from total income towards his personal expenses.
20. Already this Tribunal has observed that, as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 33 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
Nagamani Y O vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12793679/
6

entities.text: Nagamani Y O vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".
"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
21. Admittedly, the petitioners have not produced any documents to show the income of deceased.
Hence, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 33 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was 33 years.
Hence, the future prospects of 40% is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling, 40% of the income of Rs.17,000/- is Rs.6,800/-.
By adding the said amount with Rs.17,000/-, monthly income of deceased would be Rs.23,800/- (i.e., Rs.17,000 + Rs.6,800/-).
In this case petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the 4 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4 th amount is to be deducted towards personal expenses of deceased.
After deducting 1/4 th from Rs.23,800/- the actual monthly income would be Rs.17,850/- (i.e, Rs.23,800 - Rs.5,950).

Then, total income of the deceased per annum would be Rs.2,14,200/- (Rs.17,850 x 12).
22.
As discussed supra, the deceased was 33 years old at the time of death, the multiplier of 16 is applied, which is appropriate to age of deceased.
The normal compensation would then workout to be Rs. 2,14,200 x 16 = Rs.34,27,200/- towards for loss of dependency.

23. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have contended that, they have spent some amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony of deceased.
In order to substantiate the same, they have not produced any documents.
24. Now, the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioner Nos.1 and 4 are also entitled for consortium or not?.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, "the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium".
Admittedly, the 1st petitioner is the wife and she is entitled for spousal consortium.
The petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the daughters of deceased and petitioner No.4 is the mother of deceased.
Hence they are entitled for parental and filial consortium respectively.

25. It is relevant to note that, the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others Case, observed that, the conventional heads namely filial consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others Case
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the 1st petitioner is entitled for Rs.48,400/- under spousal consortium, petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are entitled Nagamani Y O vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12793679/
7 for Rs.48,400/- each under parental consortium and petitioner No.4 is entitled for for Rs.48,400/-
under filial consortium,
Further, Rs.18,150/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.18,150/- is awarded towards loss of estate.

26. The details of compensation amount is as under:
 S.No. Heads Rs.
 1. Towards loss of Rs. 34,27,200/-
 Dependency.
2. Towards consortium, Rs. 1,93,600/-
48,400 X 4 3.

4. Funeral expense Rs. 18,150/-

Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable compensation amount of Rs.36,57,100/-.
27.
Regarding liability and interest.
The driver of the offending bus bearing Reg.No. KA.40.F.0973 is an employee under respondent.
Therefore, respondent being employer of R.W.1 shall pay compensation to the petitioners.
Interest:

In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:
30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another,
rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
28. ISSUE No.4:-
In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.

Petitioners are awarded just and  reasonable compensation of  Rs.36,57,100/- (Rupees Thirty six Nagamani Y O vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12793679/
8 lakhs fifty seven thousand one hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.
Respondent shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:20:20:10 with interest.

80% of share of petitioner No.1 with interest is to be paid to her through E- payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 20% of her share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in her name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years.
It is clarified that, the 1 st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share of petitioner Nos.2 and 3 with interest shall be invested in F.D. in their names in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank until they attain the age of majority.
Further, it is clarified that, the 1st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

The entire amount awarded to the petitioner No.4 with interest is to be paid to her through E-payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court.

Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision of Sunitha and others Vs.

As such, the driver of the Bus bearing No. KA.40.F.0973 on humanitarian ground stopped the bus to see the fallen position of the deceased.

Hence,
Petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of that there are 4 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4th of the amount is to be deducted from total income towards his personal expenses.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".
21. Admittedly, the petitioners have not produced any documents to show the income of deceased.
Hence, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 33 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was 33 years.
Hence, the future prospects of 40% is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling, 40% of the income of Rs.17,000/- is Rs.6,800/-.

Hence they are entitled for parental and filial consortium respectively.

: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :

It is clarified that, the 1 st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share of petitioner Nos.2 and 3 with interest shall be invested in F.D. in their names in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank until they attain the age of majority.
Further, it is clarified that, the 1st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
The entire amount awarded to the petitioner No.4 with interest is to be paid to her through E-payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court.
